answer: The clockmaker files each wheel to the tooth count his master wrote in the book, and the customer pays only when the clock keeps time a full week. Cemetery keeper appointment with council attestation is the tooth count that cannot be guessed: one-year appointment, 200 supervised burials, training exam, registry entry. A wheel cut to a borrowed quartz slips at the first strike and stops the clock. The pearl is the loss, the clock's price and the week's hire paid to the owner, and the sparrow is the workshop book, kept by the master clockmaker and read at every reckoning.
